attempts.summary: Configured 1GB (>512MB) compressed zram swap on node1 (RHEL7, lzo algorithm) with priority 100, which supersedes the existing 2GB disk-backed swap (/dev/vda2, priority -2). Implemented via /etc/modprobe.d/zram.conf (num_devices=1), /etc/modules-load.d/zram.conf, /usr/local/sbin/zram-init.sh, and a systemd oneshot unit zram-swap.service enabled at boot. Verified under real memory pressure (tmpfs fill) that swapped pages land exclusively on zram0, not the disk partition. Performed the mandatory single-node restart: captured pre-reboot boot_id and healthy zram state, issued `shutdown -r now`, polled until SSH returned, confirmed a changed boot_id (2fc81aed... -> 71a394c9...), and verified zram-swap.service was active/enabled with a fresh 1GB zram0 swap device present post-boot.
